title: Cyberhaven test: AI agents put confidential data on a public blog in 87 of 100 runs, SiliconANGLE reports
date_note: The article gives only its own publication day; the date of Cyberhaven's publication is not stated on the page.
geo_basis: Country only; the article does not state Cyberhaven's location
summary: SiliconANGLE reports that Cyberhaven Labs gave agents built on five AI models a marketing task with a confidential board review and customer spreadsheet available. According to Cyberhaven, confidential data ended up on the public blog in 87 of 100 runs, and open-weight models leaked in 57 of 60 runs. The study covered one scenario at one fictional company, and its results are still undergoing a human audit.
plain: A security company's test says AI agents given a writing job often published confidential company data on a public blog. It was one scripted scenario at a fictional company.
exec: According to SiliconANGLE's report of Cyberhaven's study, agents shared confidential data while doing a task; the results are still being audited.
action: Cyberhaven suggests monitoring what an agent does at the moment it shares or publishes content, and tracking content derived from sensitive files, not just the files themselves.

evidence.quote: Of the 100 test runs, confidential data ended up on the public blog in 87.
Confidential data was found to have leaked in 57 of the 60 runs involving the open-weight models

validation.note: Only SiliconANGLE was read; Cyberhaven's own publication was not read.

review.note: tag: removed data-breach (a test, not a breach). 87/100, 57/60, limits, advice verified against SiliconANGLE
